newsitem.title: USA: New York threat to Swiss banks seen as uncertain.
newsitem.headline: New York threat to Swiss banks seen as uncertain.

text.p: Banking industry sources on Wednesday said they were uncertain about the potential impact on Swiss banks from possible curbs by the state of New York and New York City.
But it appeared talk of ending New York City deposits in Swiss banks would have a negligible effect. A source at one Swiss bank said very little money was involved.

The New York State Banking Department, which regulates about 200 foreign bank branches and agencies, including eight Swiss-based banks and representative offices, said it was reviewing a proposal by a state lawmaker.
The proposal would amend the state banking law to require an independent audit of accounts opened by Holocaust victims and protect dormant accounts.
Separately, a bill was introduced in the New York City council which would stop the city from depositing money in Swiss banks until the Swiss government set up a compensation fund.
A spokesman for a group of Swiss banks in New York was unable to provide any figures on deposits.

A spokesman for the New York City Comptroller said that as of January 29, the city had approximately $4.5 billion of cash, out of which $225 million is invested in short-term instruments with Credit Suisse First Boston.
About half of that sum held by the Swiss bank matures on January 30, with the rest maturing next week.
The spokesman said there were no deposit accounts at Swiss banks.
The New York State Banking Department regulates eight Swiss institutions, including the big three of Swiss banking, Union Bank of Switzerland, CS Holding's Credit Suisse and Swiss Bank Corp.
